### Observed differences

- The choice of what follows activity A05 shifted between the windows: in the earlier window, among A05's observed outgoing transitions, about 42 in 100 led to A03, about 31 to A09 and about 27 to A04; in the later window, only about 23 in 100 led to A03, while A04 received about 41 in 100 and A09 about 35 in 100 — A03 lost roughly 18 percentage points, taken up mainly by A04 (+14 points) [DIR001].
- This rests on 96 observed outgoing transitions of A05 in the earlier window and 111 in the later one; the overall magnitude is modest (cosine dissimilarity about 0.08), but it was larger than in about 99.5% of random re-splits of the pooled traces [DIR001].
- All three successors (A03, A04, A09) were observed in both windows, so this is a redistribution between existing alternatives rather than the appearance or disappearance of a path [DIR001].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence
The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Only one control-flow item qualified out of 56 tested units, where about 0.28 items would be expected by chance in an unchanged process, so the apparent rerouting after A05 — A03 ceding share to A04 and A09 — is a count of the same order as the chance expectation and cannot be distinguished from sampling variation, however unusual the single item looks [DIR001].

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

The evidence contains:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after
- Screening: 72 units tested, 0.29 items expected without change
  - Control flow: 56 units tested, 1 item, 0.28 expected
  - Time: 16 units tested, 0 items, 0.008 expected
- One evidence item: DIR001

DIR001: CF_DIR indicator on activity A05. Outgoing transition shares from A05:
- Before: A03 ≈ 0.42, A09 ≈ 0.31, A04 ≈ 0.27
- After: A03 ≈ 0.23, A09 ≈ 0.35, A04 ≈ 0.41
- Differences: A03 -0.18, A04 +0.14, A09 +0.04
- observed_change (cosine dissimilarity) ≈ 0.08
- empirical_strength ≈ 0.995 (99.5% of reference comparisons had smaller difference)
- Support: 96 outgoing transitions observed before, 111 after

So the behaviour: after A05 completes, the next activity was A03 in about 42 in 100 transitions before, dropping to about 23 in 100 after; A04 rose from about 27 to 41 in 100; A09 rose slightly from 31 to 35.

Now the judgement. The instructions say:

"First compare the number of evidence items with the number expected by chance, per family when screening.by_family is present. A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

Control flow family: 1 item, 0.28 expected without change. One item when fewer than one is expected — this is exactly the example given: "one or two items when fewer than one is expected" is what an unchanged process typically produces. So we must choose "Insufficient evidence".

Time family: 0 items, 0.008 expected — nothing there.

So the support level is "Insufficient evidence". Even though the single DIR item has empirical_strength 0.995, the screening comparison says one item when 0.28 expected is typical of an unchanged process.

The answer format:

### Observed differences
Describe the DIR001 finding: routing after A05 redistributed. Before: of the outgoing transitions of A05, ~42% went to A03, ~31% to A09, ~27% to A04. After: ~23% to A03, ~35% to A09, ~41% to A04. Support: 96 transitions before, 111 after. Empirical strength 99.5% — unusual for random splits, but a single item.

No time items, no resource items, no OCC/POS/REL/LAG. So only control flow.

### Inference
"Support level: Insufficient evidence"
"The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process." Plus one short sentence on the limitation: the single control-flow item matches what an unchanged process typically produces (1 item vs ~0.28 expected by chance across 56 tested units), so the routing shift after A05 cannot be distinguished from sampling variation despite its high empirical strength.

I could fold the screening comparison into the inference paragraph and cite [DIR001] since the item count relates to it. Actually the screening block is part of the evidence; identifiers available: only DIR001. I'll cite [DIR001] on bullets describing the DIR finding, and for the screening sentence in the inference, I can cite [DIR001] as well since it's about that item qualifying. That seems reasonable.

Also: "Always compare the two windows: for each difference, state what the behaviour looked like in the earlier window as well as in the later one." Done.

Rounded percentages: A03 42% → 23%, A04 27% → 41%, A09 31% → 35%. Support 96 vs 111 outgoing transitions.
